audit.summary: The printed raw-cosine log objective is undefined on admissible embeddings. Retaining its actual negative sign and inserting a sigmoid still leaves a materially different positive-class weighting in the release. The earlier missing-minus allegation is withdrawn. Separate Minor catalog-selection defect.
limitations: P1 — The stated optimization objective is undefined on allowed embeddings and differs materially from the released loss — Counterevidence: The published equation already has a conventional negative sign; the previous contrary reading was caused by a missing glyph in the initial raster and is withdrawn. The source applies the negative sign at trainer.py232 and sigmoids at214-215, so this check does not imply released training produces NaNs. An implicit sigmoid interpretation would repair the domain but conflicts with the explicit ordinary-cosine definition and still omits positive reweighting. If P=N, the weight is one; the multi-answer task with N=100 does not require P=N. The complete embedding-to-loss path uses LayerNorm followed by unconstrained affine representation layers (model.py64,75,86,102,111; applied255-265 before concatenation267), with the same affine maps for item embeddings at trainer.py183-194. No final positivity constraint precedes CosineSimilarity at trainer.py62,213. Recovery source-page inspection confirms the negative prefactor, ordinary cosine definition, and lack of sigmoid and class weights.

P2 — The released negative sampler overwrites the contemporaneous product catalog — Counterevidence: If every month has identical item membership, this bug is dormant. If the intended evaluation deliberately uses a fixed global catalog, no temporal lookup is needed, but that is not the stated monthly-availability convention and does not explain the penultimate-month behavior after the last date. Missing historical source provenance prevents attributing numerical benchmark damage. This is separate from the TST module's relative positional alignment and does not refute its attention-mask design.

proposition.claim:
Section 3.4, PDF p.6, defines cos(z_output,y^k) as ordinary cosine similarity. Eq.(8) has the conventional NEGATIVE prefactor -1/|K_gt union K_n|. It omits a sigmoid, another probability conversion, a positivity restriction and positive-class reweighting, and is stated to drive training. The minus is visible in the reliable PyMuPDF recovery rendering of the same original page.

Appendix O.4, p.21, states that monthly product lists are beginning-of-month availability snapshots used with purchase dates to determine which products can be offered. mainfinal.py lines116-135 loads lists in sorted filename order; dataloader.py lines33-39 converts their keys to corresponding first-of-month dates. The sampler comments that it selects the candidate products during the purchase date (lines201-209), but its loop overwrites the selection through the final month.
proposition.domain: Completed report for I25-43526; exact inspected scope and limitations are retained in the report and coverage ledger.
assumptions: Nonzero real output and item vectors, the domain needed for ordinary cosine similarity; no nonnegativity condition is imposed.
A positive-item set and negative-item set with disjoint item identities; distinct items may have coinciding learned embeddings because no injectivity condition is imposed.
For the source comparison P=|K_gt|>0 and N=|K_n|; the default N=100 is explicit in parameters.py line72, and P=2 is allowed by the multi-label task.

For the unweighted-versus-source minimizer comparison, retain the printed conventional negative sign and insert a sigmoid probability link; this comparator repairs the cosine-domain defect but not the released class weighting.
Monthly snapshots have increasing dates, as produced by sorted YYMM filenames and preserved dictionary insertion order.
Purchase date lies after the first snapshot and before a later snapshot.
There are at least 100 unseen candidates in each relevant example pool, with no duplicates; positive item IDs and browsing-history IDs are excluded as the sampler requires.
The diagnosis is for the pinned source; no claim is made that this exact source produced the paper's experiments.

repair.content:
A source-aligned corrected statement is the weighted sigmoid BCE formula L_src above, for nonzero embeddings and P,N>0. The analytic check shows it is finite for cosine scores and matches the static weighting structure for one sequence. This is not a claim that this was the historical experimental loss. If the intended method is instead ordinary unweighted sigmoid BCE, the source must be reconciled and experimental provenance supplied; fresh training may be necessary to determine the difference.

Withdraw missing-minus allegation; original Eq.(8) is negative. Domain and class-weight arguments and all numerical results are unchanged.

For sorted snapshot dates d_0<...<d_{M-1} and a session t>=d_0, select j=max{i:d_i<=t} once, then use catalog_j. Explicitly handle sessions before d_0 and insufficient eligible negatives. This selects February for the finite example and can be proved from the definition of beginning-of-month snapshots; historical benchmark changes require replaying original sampling/evaluation.
